questions.q: What is one of the two most common real-world causes of duplicate CIs named in this lesson?
options: A manual CI entry that Discovery later fails to match, creating a second record instead of updating the first
Running Discovery too frequently against the same CI class
A CI Health Dashboard score being too high
A CI class having too many relationships defined
questions.explain: A timing and matching gap between manual entry and later Discovery is one of the two leading real-world causes, alongside a loose Identification Rule.

questions.q: What role does duplicate-detection reporting play in cleanup?
options: It replaces the need for an Identification Rule entirely
It surfaces likely-duplicate pairs by comparing attributes, for a human to review before anything is consolidated
It automatically deletes any record it flags as a duplicate
It permanently locks a CI record from future edits
questions.explain: Detection is deliberately a review step -- a person confirms a genuine match before any consolidation happens.

questions.q: Why is merging the correct fix for a confirmed duplicate pair, rather than deleting one record?
options: ServiceNow technically does not allow deleting any CI record
Merging and deleting produce identical results in every case
Merging is actually slower and riskier than deleting a duplicate
Deleting orphans relationships and loses Incident/Change history silently, while merging consolidates that history onto the surviving CI
questions.explain: A CI accumulates real history almost immediately -- deleting it loses that history with no error raised, while merging preserves it.

questions.q: What specifically gets lost if a duplicate CI is simply deleted instead of merged?
options: The Identification Rule itself is deleted along with the CI
Nothing -- deleting a duplicate CI has no downstream effect
Only the CI's display name, which can be easily re-entered
Relationships, Incident/Change history, and other references pointing at the deleted record
questions.explain: Those references become orphaned when the record they point to disappears, and the failure is silent rather than raising an error.

questions.q: After merging a confirmed duplicate pair, what should happen next per this lesson's full cleanup loop?
options: Fix the Identification Rule that allowed the duplication, so it doesn't recur on the next Discovery run
Disable Discovery permanently for that CI class
Nothing further is needed once a merge is complete
Immediately delete the surviving CI as well, for consistency
questions.explain: Merging treats the existing symptom; tightening the Identification Rule is what actually prevents the same duplication from happening again.
